---
applyTo: '.github/workflows/*.yml'
---

# Workflow Notes for AI Agents

## .github/workflows/

- `CI.yml` covers the same ground as local `make check` (which runs `make tidy`, the pre-commit hooks, and tests), but fans it out across four parallel jobs: `secrets` (trufflehog, then `nox -s secrets` on the staged change), `precommit` (`nox -s precommit`), `analysis` (`nox -s analysis`, which runs the `ty`, `basedpyright` and `pylint` hooks) and `pytest` (`nox -s test`). The analysis hooks are the slowest in the config, so they have their own job rather than lengthening `precommit`, the job the run waits on. CI still runs `.github/scripts/ci-ruff-args.sh` before the pre-commit session to modify ruff args for stricter checking and GitHub-optimized output formatting, while local `make check` uses the default args from `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- **`run-ci` (`Run CI (3.13)`) and `checks` are the contexts `main` requires, through the ruleset `main-protect`, and their names are load-bearing.** Renaming the job leaves a required context that never reports, which blocks every pull request, and renaming it to something not required silently un-gates the branch. Check `gh api repos/michen00/freeze-pr-links/rulesets` before touching it. `dependabot-auto-merge.yml` names the same context and enables auto-merge only while a ruleset requires it, so rename both together. The job set can otherwise grow freely behind it.
- **No hook may pass by scanning nothing.** gitleaks reads only staged changes, so under `pre-commit run --all-files` on a clean checkout it scans nothing and passes. The `precommit` job skips it, and the `secrets` job resets the checkout softly to the comparison base (the pull request's base, or the commit before a push), so the whole change is staged, then runs `nox -s secrets`, which fails when nothing is staged rather than passing. `tests/test_ci_jobs.py` checks that the job stages before it scans. A dispatched run has no base, so only trufflehog scans it. talisman was removed for the same reason: its pre-push hook reads the pushed refs from stdin, which pre-commit does not pass on, so it scanned nothing locally or in CI, and run on the staged change it flagged 29 of main's last 40 pull requests with no real secret among them.
- ty, basedpyright and pylint run in the `analysis` job, through their pre-commit hooks at the default stage, and the `precommit` job skips them with `SKIP`. That `SKIP` names the hook ids in `noxfile.py`'s `_ANALYSIS_HOOKS` and `_SECRET_HOOKS`, and `tests/test_ci_jobs.py` fails if they part. The ty hook syncs `uv.lock`, with every dependency group, into the project environment and checks against it, so no second dependency list is kept; ty's version comes from the hook's `rev`, not from `uv.lock`. basedpyright and pylint run as local hooks through `uv run --locked --all-groups`, so their versions come from `uv.lock`, and `pyrightconfig.json` and `.pylintrc` enable only the checks ruff and ty do not make.
- `pr-mechanical-checks.yml` is the deterministic gate on the pull request title, its body (the Summary and Testing sections, and template leftovers) and the branch's commit subjects; its job is `checks`. It is read-only (`contents: read`) and runs the stdlib-only modules in `checks/` on a bare interpreter, with no project install. Each check records its errors and warnings to files, which the job uploads as the `pr-advisory-findings` artifact, even when empty.
- **Coverage comment.** CI's `pytest` job also writes a coverage JSON, diffs the branch against its comparison base, renders `coverage/report.md` with `scripts/coverage_diff_report.py` (how many of the changed lines a test ran, else the repository totals), and uploads it as the `coverage-report` artifact. `coverage-comment.yml` runs on `workflow_run` after CI, from `main`'s copy, resolves the pull request from the run's head SHA, and has `.github/scripts/coverage-comment.sh` keep one coverage comment on it. `coverage-on-demand.yml` measures a pull request again when a member or collaborator comments `/coverage-report` on it, or by dispatch, and replaces that comment. Nothing fails on a coverage number. The `workflow_run` and comment-triggered workflows take effect only once merged, so their tests are the pre-merge evidence.
- `pr-advisory-comment.yml` runs on `workflow_run` after the gate, so GitHub takes its definition from `main` and a pull request cannot rewrite the `pull-requests: write` scope it holds. It downloads the findings, resolves the pull request from the run's head SHA rather than from anything in the artifact, and runs `.github/scripts/pr-findings-comment.sh`. That script keeps one comment on the pull request: why the checks failed first, then the advisory warnings. It updates the comment as the pull request changes and deletes it once nothing is left. A change to it takes effect only once merged, so `tests/test_pr_advisory_comment_workflow.py` and `tests/test_pr_findings_comment.py` are its pre-merge evidence.
- `freeze-pr-links.yml` runs this repository's own action on `pull_request_target` when a pull request merges. It checks out the default branch and runs `action.yml` from it, so nothing from the pull request runs; `tests/test_workflows.py` pins that, and that `action.yml` checks nothing out. [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md) lists the properties the action keeps.
- `pr-catchup.yml` runs on every push to `main` and on a manual dispatch from `main`. It merges `main` into each open, same-repository pull request that is behind and does not conflict, through the REST merge call, with the commit subject `chore: merge main into #N`. GitHub holds the pull_request runs such a commit causes until someone with write access approves them, because github-actions[bot] made it. The workflow approves only the runs at the commit it pushed, with the predicate in `.github/scripts/approve-bot-gated-runs.sh`, and fails if any run stays held, if no run appears, or if a merge is refused for a reason other than a conflict. A Dependabot merge does not start it, because `dependabot-auto-merge.yml` enables auto-merge with GITHUB_TOKEN and GitHub creates no workflow run for an event that token caused; `gh workflow run pr-catchup.yml` catches the branches up after one. Setting `vars.APP_CLIENT_ID` and `secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY` makes it merge as that App instead, so GitHub holds none of the runs its merges cause; Dependabot merges would start it only if `dependabot-auto-merge.yml` also enabled auto-merge with an App token.
- Cache resets rely on a new `.github/workflows/.cache-buster` (see `make bust-ci-cache`, which writes the time and a random UUID, so no two busts match). That file is folded into every cache key, so a new one invalidates them all, and `tests/test_workflow_caches.py` fails if a cache leaves it out. The pre-commit caches lead with the buster, then the hook config: a changed config restores the newest entry under the same buster through `restore-keys`, so only the hooks whose rev moved are built again, and `pre-commit gc` drops what the config no longer uses before the entry is saved. A new buster matches no entry and starts from empty. `coverage-on-demand.yml` keeps no uv cache, since it runs rarely and setup-uv's default key would leave the buster out. Each job keeps its own uv cache entry (`cache-suffix: ${{ github.job }}`), because the jobs install different dependency groups and an existing key is never saved again: with one shared key, the first job to finish would save and the others would download what it lacked on every run. Each job installs only the `ci` dependency group (nox and pre-commit) for itself. The `test` session installs its own group; the `precommit` and `analysis` sessions make no environment of their own and run pre-commit from the `ci` one.
- Hook version bumps are Dependabot's job via the `pre-commit` ecosystem in `.github/dependabot.yml`.
- `release.yml` publishes a GitHub release when a `vX.Y.Z` tag is pushed, and `changelog-autoupdate.yml`, run by dispatch, opens a pull request that regenerates CHANGELOG.md's Unreleased section from the commits on `main`; RELEASING.md describes the flow. `greet-new-contributors.yml` welcomes a first-time contributor.
- `lint-github-actions.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only: actionlint is already enforced on every pull request into `main` and every push to `main` by its pinned pre-commit hook, which CI runs. Keep the workflow's pinned image tag in step with the hook's `rev`.
- **Documentation Consistency:** Keep guidance documents (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/instructions/CI.instructions.md`, `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, and `README.md`) consistent with workflow behavior, and change them in the same commit as the workflow.
